subject: Re: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment — hardware & offline ops follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@legacybank.com>, John Rivera <john.rivera@legacybank.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-28T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — On-prem / air-gapped qualification

Hi Alice / John,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the on-prem, air-gapped deployment properly: 

What we heard:
- You need a fully air-gapped Private deployment inside Legacy Bank data centers (no outbound internet from inference nodes).
- Target workload: low-latency customer-facing inference for document understanding (~1000 QPS peak, average 40k tokens/min).
- Expectation: offline maintenance windows, controlled hardware upgrades, strict change control and audit logs.

Open items for scoping (please confirm):
1) Hardware baseline: do you plan to provision a new GPU cluster or reuse existing EOL servers? If new, preferred GPU type (A10/A100/H100) and target node count.
2) Storage & networking: preferred SAN/NAS vs local NVMe; expected model storage (TBs) and retention for binaries/artifacts.
3) Offline ops: how do you handle physical transport of media for upgrades (sneakernet) vs removable drives vs controlled VPN windows?
4) Maintenance windows & on-call: your preferred weekly/monthly windows and escalation contacts.

Attachments: I attached our on-prem hardware checklist and a starter runbook we use for air-gapped installs (redwood-onprem-hw-specs.pdf, network-checklist.xlsx).

Next steps: if you can reply with the answers above and confirm the infra POC (who will own the hardware/ops side), we’ll schedule a 60-min ops deep-dive next week to align on installer approach and any procurement constraints. Proposed slots: Tue Jul 12 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed Jul 13 14:00-15:00 PT.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk through the checklist.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference


From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@legacybank.com>

Cc: John Rivera <john.rivera@legacybank.com>
Date: 2027-07-01T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — On-prem / air-gapped qualification

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and checklist. A few quick answers while I pull folks together: 

1) Hardware: procurement is planning for a refresh — we'll likely standardize on A100 systems (we have existing A10 but want to standardize). Initial ask is for 8 GPUs, but that may scale to 16 based on your throughput guidance.
2) Storage: we'll provision NVMe local on the nodes for model cache and a separate SAN for long-term artifacts. Estimate initially 10 TB usable for models.
3) Offline ops: we prefer controlled removable drives for major upgrades (sneakernet is acceptable under change control), and we can allow an outbound management jump box only during approved maintenance windows.
4) Windows & on-call: typical maintenance window is Saturday 02:00-06:00 local time; I'll share the infra ops POC (Miguel Santos) below.

I've copied John who owns procurement and Miguel will be looped for the ops call. Please send over the final runbook and we will review with our security/compliance team.

Best,
Alice
Director, AI Platform — Legacy Bank

---
Alice Morgan
Legacy Bank

Thanks Alice — helpful. Attaching three artifacts: redwood-onprem-hw-specs.pdf (recommended node configs and GPU options), network-checklist.xlsx (air-gap network & jump-box checklist), and a draft redwood-onprem-runbook.docx (installer steps & rollback).

Couple of clarifying Qs for Miguel / procurement so the ops call can be productive: 
- If you provision 8 A100 GPUs initially, do you have a preferred rack density (e.g., 4x A100 per 1U/2U nodes) or will we assume standard 2 GPUs per host? Our recommended baseline for ~1000 QPS at 8 GPUs is 2 GPUs/host (4 hosts) with NVMe cache, but we can optimize further at deploy time.
- For the removable-media upgrade approach: do you have an internal secure vault policy for media handoff and scanned integrity checks? We can support signed images and an offline verification step in the runbook.
- For compliance artifacts: is there a dedicated SSO/IdP audit channel we should integrate for installer auth, or will you provide temporary service accounts during maintenance windows?

I've also added a HubSpot link for scheduling and scoping: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345678

Proposed ops call: Tue Jul 12 10:00-11:00 PT — please confirm. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and include a short agenda (installer handoff, acceptance criteria, SLAs and pricing overview).

—
Marissa
